info.title: SecurityScorecard API
info.description:
SecurityScorecard enables users to instantly rate and understand the security
risk of any company. Users can view and monitor security ratings, easily add
vendors or partner organizations, and report on the cyberhealth of their
ecosystem. It also provides access to analytics,
compliance frameworks, collaboration, digital asset management, and other tools that
help enterprises better manage security and meet compliance objectives.

This document describes the SecurityScorecard API that is available along with
the [SecurityScorecard platform](https://platform.securityscorecard.io).
API endpoints are configured on a per client basis, and individual endpoints
may vary based on the agreement with the client. This document contains all
possible endpoints.

For technical support please contact us at
[support@securityscorecard.io](support@securityscorecard.io). We typically
respond in 48 hours and operate Monday thru Friday 9am - 5pm EST (excluding
US federal holidays).

## Schema

All API access is over HTTPS. All data is sent and received as JSON unless specified otherwise.

## Upgrades and Backwards compatibility

All resources and representations are maintained in a backwards compatible manner
(please see the section below for what are considered backward compatible changes).
If any url or schema is updated in a future version, support for all pre-existent operations and schemas
is preserved to ensure backwards compatibility.

This means that if a program is written against a version of our API, you can expect it will continue to work
against future versions if implemented with the considerations detailed below.

### Evolving scorecard issue types and factors

A very important exception to endpoint stability is that given our continuously evolving set of
scorecard issue types and factors,
endpoints specific to each of them might change as new type of security signals are added (or retired)
from SecurityScorecard, or the specific attributes associated to their findings evolve.

In order to ensure integrations are prepared for this, it's important you use the endpoints available
to determine the
[existing issue types](https://platform.securityscorecard.io/docs/index.html#tag/metadata/paths/~1metadata~1issue-types/get)
or simply navigate to specific issue types using link urls in parent responses,
eg. see `detail_url` for scorecard issues
[here](https://platform.securityscorecard.io/docs/index.html#tag/scores/paths/~1companies~1{scorecard_identifier}/get),
avoiding for example relying on a fixed list of issue types.

### What is considered a non-breaking or backward compatible change?

All our API operations and schemas are kept backward compatible to ensure:
- all existing requests working against the current version will continue to work in the future
- all the responses continue to include the same information included currently, but can include additional
new properties anywhere in the json response, that should be ignored or omitted on deserialization.

With this criteria, these are considered non-breaking or backward compatible changes:
- new endpoints
- new optional parameters:
  - query parameters
  - new optional properties in any part of a json request body
  - new optional request http headers
- new supported values of these request parameters
- new properties in any part of a json response body
- new response http headers
  - this can include a pagination `Link` header, added to collections that after reaching
a very large size we might need to introduce a fixed page size, see Pagination section.
- changes to the length or format of entity IDs or other opaque strings.
- issue types or factors being added, retired (if deemed obsolete as security signals),
or changes to their associated severity and details
- new event types in [event logs](https://platform.securityscorecard.io/docs/index.html#tag/event-log)
(your code should ignore or gracefully handle unfamiliar event types)

And these would be considered breaking changes:
- retiring existing endpoints
- new required parameters
- retiring support for values of these request parameters
- retiring properties in any part of a json response body
- modifying the type or meaning of existing properties
- retiring response http headers
- changes to expected http status codes

### Additional properties in json responses

In most tech stacks this a non-issue and already contemplated in json libraries, but here are some references
to special cases:
- In java, when using jackson serializer set `FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES` to `false`,
an example from swagger's official API client generator is
shown [here](https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/blob/0eb385c0d6497c38c09b42158b2d66109b78b15b/samples/server/petstore/jaxrs/jersey1-useTags/src/gen/java/org/openapitools/api/JacksonJsonProvider.java#L22)

### Breaking Changes

While we're committed to keep all existing endpoints backward compatible it is possible a specific
feature or functionality is retired from our product, whenever this happens:
- we'll notify customers with a notice of 3 months minimum
- we'll publish the event in this section
- we'll provide assistance detailing a migration path if one is available

## Common Responses

### 400 Bad Request

Sending a request with invalid json or that doesn't satisfy requirements specified in
this documentation will result in this error.

### 401 Unauthorized

An access token is missing or invalid, see [Authentication](#section/Authentication) section
about how to authenticate your requests.

### 403 Forbidden

The authenticated user has no permission to perform this operation.

Some common causes for this are:
 - your account doesn't have API access enabled
 - your account doesn't have a specific feature enabled that is required for the operation
 - the operation requires a user with higher access level
 - the operation is trying access or modify a resource owned by another user or organization
(in some cases a 404 might be used instead to avoid revealing existence of private information)

## Scorecard Identifiers

In many endpoints that are specific to a scorecard or company, we support multiple ways to specify a
scorecard identifier for your convenience.

Accepted identifiers are the following:
  - primary domain. eg. `securityscorecard.com`. this is the primary internet domain associated
  with a scorecard, you can find these in the response to adding a company to a portfolio, or in
  the list of a portfolio's contents.
  - id, these universal unique identifiers are associated to each of our scorecards, and are also available
  after adding one to a portfolio,
  or when obtaining the contents of an existing portfolio.

## Pagination

Requests that support pagination respond with a [Link](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5988) http header.

When pagination is supported a link to "next" is included, unless on the last page
(use this to determine the end of the collection).

```
Link: <https://api.securityscorecard.io/companies/example.com/...>; rel="next"
```

It's very important to follow these urls to traverse collections instead of
constructing urls on your own. Doing so will protect your integration from
future changes.

In some cases when a collection exceeds a certain size, we'll offer instead a report
to asynchronously generate a dump of the entire collection.
An example of this is the
[full scorecard report](https://platform.securityscorecard.io/docs/index.html#tag/reports/paths/~1reports~1full-scorecard-json/post)
that offers the entire collection of issue findings on a scorecard.

## Rate Limiting

For API requests done with an access token, you can make up to 5000 requests
per hour per user. If an operation has a different limit it will be specified
on the description of the operation below.

If you reach the limit you'll be temporarily blocked and receive a response with:

- http 429 status
- [Retry-After](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Retry-After) http header
indicating the seconds to wait until next request.

## Bot Users

Bot users are API access only accounts that enable customers to spread out their API usage
to multiple accounts without having to associate them to real employee accounts.
Multiple bot API tokens can be managed by administrators at your account's
[users list](https://platform.securityscorecard.io/#/my-settings/users) without the need to login with different accounts.

This is beneficial especially for customers who use our SSO capability, for customers who use one
of our [integrations](https://securityscorecard.com/hub/integrations), or have built out
their own production ready applications.

Creating a bot user requires admin access and you can follow the following steps
in the [SecurityScorecard platform](https://platform.securityscorecard.io):

1 - Go through the normal process of adding a new user but on the top right check the checkbox
to indicate that it's a bot and then set the name and permissions

<img src="https://api.securityscorecard.io/docs/images/bot-user-add.png" />

2 - Search for the user you just created in the list and generate a new token

<img src="https://api.securityscorecard.io/docs/images/bot-user-search.png" />

3 - Once a token is generated, copy it and keep it safe

<img src="https://api.securityscorecard.io/docs/images/bot-user-generated-token.png" />

Admins can generate new tokens for a bot user at any time in the future but please note that
the previous token will be automatically revoked



## Code Samples

### Portfolios - Add a Company

In the following example we identify the default private portfolio, then
we add a company to that portfolio



```python

import os
import requests
import sys

token = os.getenv('SSC_API_TOKEN')
api_url = os.getenv('API_URL', 'https://api.securityscorecard.io')

headers = {
    'Accept': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'Authorization': 'Token ' + token,
    'cache-control': 'no-cache',
    }

# get portfolios
url = api_url + '/portfolios'
response = requests.get(api_url + '/portfolios', headers=headers)
response.raise_for_status()

portfolios = response.json()['entries']
my_portfolio = [
    item for item in portfolios
    # My Portfolio is read_only and private
    if 'read_only' in item and item['read_only'] == True and item['privacy'] == 'private'
][0]

# add google.com to the portfolio
url = api_url + '/portfolios/' + my_portfolio['id'] + '/companies/google.com'
response = requests.put(url, headers=headers)
response.raise_for_status()

# get scorecards in My Portfolio
url = api_url + '/portfolios/' + my_portfolio['id'] + '/companies'
response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
response.raise_for_status()

scorecards = response.json()['entries']

# check google.com is in the portfolio
scorecard = [
    item for item in scorecards
    if item['domain'] == 'google.com'
]
assert len(scorecard) == 1, 'scorecard not found in the portfolio'

print ('google.com score is ' + str(scorecard[0]['score']))


```



At the end of the example we assert that the company was truly added to
the default private portfolio

Token.description:
SecurityScorecard API endpoints require an authentication token to be passed
in an authorization header in order to return data. If you do not already
have a token, you can create one by going to the API Access area in your
[Settings page](https://platform.securityscorecard.io/#/settings/api) and then
clicking Generate New Token. Please note this tokens have no expiration
so they can be used until manually revoked. If you have a token and generate
a new one, the previous token will be revoked and can no longer be used.

Administrators can also revoke API tokens for any user in their account.

Once you have your token you can pass it in using the `Authorization` http header like this:

```
curl -X GET \
  https://api.securityscorecard.io/portfolios \
  -H 'authorization: Token <your token>'
```

event_type.description:
the type of event, at the moment one of these:
- `issues`: indicates the arrival or departure of issues to this scorecard
- `breach`: a breach was associated to this company
- `recalibration`: indicates a recalibration event

Note: additional event types might be introduced in the future.

group_status.description:
when event type is "issues" indicates
the status of the associated group of issues, at the moment one of:
- `active`: new issues have been observed
- `resolved`: issues were refuted and resolution confirmed by SecurityScorecard
- `departed`: issues are not observed anymore

issue_count.description:
when event type is "issues" indicates
the number of issue findings associated to this event

total_score_impact.description:
total score impact of the findings detected in the event, to
the company's overall score

issue_type.description:
when event type is "issues" indicates
the type of the associated issues, one of the
[existing issue types](#tag/metadata%2Fpaths%2F~1metadata~1issue-types%2Fget)

breach_data.description:
when event type is "breach" includes
additional information about the breach.

Important Note: the fields available here might change in the future.

factor.description: factor the associated issue type belongs to

detail_url.description: api endpoint to get the issue findings detail of this event
